additional_info.subject: RE: ID0460274-DC/Si-D/AT-[Y2/T10 4002926962] Voltage issue CRM:02889000831
additional_info.body:
Dear Johannes,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0460274.
This ticket, as well as ticket
ID0459972
, was opened to address a query regarding a discrepancy between the Target Voltage and the Actual Voltage during a charging session.
For sake of completeness, I am sharing below the response I previously shared with you in the other ticket:
This gap can be noticed in the logs as well, and
it is perfectly normal.
The Target Voltage (EV_TarVol) is a parameter communicated by the EV which represents the battery voltage level at 100% of SOC. The measured voltage (EVSE_NowVol) represents the instantaneous voltage at the interface between the EV and the charger, hence we can say in a certain way it is the instantaneous voltage level of the EV's battery. Therefore, there will always be a gap between these two parameters, if the SOC is not 100%, as power converters and batteries are two voltage generators in parallel. To charge the EV's battery, the charger provides a constant current, while raising the voltage level up to the Target Voltage.
Here some examples for you:
SOC not 100%:
|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=172|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=265|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=87.4|EVSE_NowCur[A]=235
|EVSE_NowVol[V]=371.6
|EV_TarCur[A]=242|
EV_TarVol[V]=430
|EV_SOC[%]=44|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=172|Pilot=4
SOC at 100%:
|EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=160|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=400|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=0|EVSE_NowCur[A]=0|
EVSE_NowVol[V]=730.7|
EV_TarCur[A]=0
|EV_TarVol[V]=733
|EV_SOC[%]=100|EVSE_DESpwr[kW]=4|Cable_Max[A]=400|Phase=5
What is important is that the Actual Current follows the Target Current request from the EV, with a discrepancy according to the standards.
Hope this explanation clarifies your doubts. If there are no further questions, I would proceed to close this query and ticket.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
